source.title: Usage-Modulated Sentiment Representations in Large Language Models
source.authors: Hong-Fei Du; Jia-Cheng Shi; Yan-Fu Zhang; Gang Zhou; Ye Gao

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study analyzes sentiment representations, not refusal behavior. Its results do not test whether a refusal direction exists or mediates refusal, and it does not rely on the refusal-direction finding to conduct its analyses.
record.gate_note: The paper cites refusal-direction work as prior research, but its measured behavior and interventions concern sentiment polarity, tone, and audience adaptation. Those results are recorded as related-construct findings, not as tests of the refusal claim. No results cited from other work are included.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes sentiment-polarity directions and tone/audience residuals in Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct and Gemma-7B-IT. It cites Arditi et al. (2024) only as prior work on concept directions and on steering refusal. It never derives, ablates or adds a refusal direction, and it measures no refusal behaviour. Its methodological analogue, a difference-in-means direction plus a structured residual, concerns sentiment, a different construct. The record's 'discusses' overstates the engagement; the refusal work is only cited.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct in substance. The authors conclude that a robust shared sentiment direction exists but does not fully characterize sentiment representations in their controlled setting. The residual variation is systematically structured by tone and audience: it is compact, reproducible across splits, and selectively erasable. Residualized tone components steer Llama output tone while preserving polarity.
record.recipe_differences: The paper estimates a shared difference-in-means direction for positive versus negative sentiment realizations, projects it out of sentiment deltas, and studies residual usage structure. It does not derive or intervene on a refusal direction, does not ablate refusal at every layer and position, and does not test refusal behavior.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported geometry varies with pooling choice and model; residual usage decoding has different layer profiles by pooling. Generation steering is evaluated at fixed layer and strength settings, with judge robustness checked using a second judge.

fits_no_version.finding: A shared difference-in-means sentiment direction is robust (held-out median cosine 0.953–0.975), but it captures only 0.172–0.301 of the squared norm of individual deltas. 0.833–0.909 of the norm remains after projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For sentiment, a single difference-in-means direction is highly aligned across conditions but leaves most per-sample representation change unexplained (a sentiment analogue of V4, not refusal).

fits_no_version.finding: Residual sentiment deltas encode tone and audience above shuffle baselines. Erasing a rank-3 residual subspace cuts usage-metric retention to 0.456–0.644, versus about 1.0 for random subspaces and 0.97–0.99 for shuffled ones.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: After a shared sentiment direction is projected out, usage-conditioned residual subspaces carry held-out tone and audience information.

fits_no_version.finding: In Llama, injecting residualized tone and audience directions shifts output style and keeps the requested polarity in 150 of 152 outputs (98.7%). The result is corroborated by a second judge and by transfer to human-written text.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residualized usage directions steer style while preserving sentiment polarity.

record.problems: The analysis uses a controlled synthetic dataset and three instruction-tuned models at 7B/8B scale. A single human annotator performed the dataset spot checks. Generation steering is limited to Llama and model-based judgments under fixed settings; the authors state it is not a complete editing method. No general-capability evaluation is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Table 4 subspace compactness and stability metrics and layer-level appendix diagnostics are not itemized; they concern sentiment usage structure rather than refusal. No refusal-related result is reported.

untested.parts: All: no refusal direction, ablation, addition, or capability check on refusal.
All: no weight-edit removal of refusal.
All: no jailbreak or adversarial-training analysis.
All for refusal; the 'direction plus residual structure' finding concerns sentiment only.
All: no harmfulness or refusal representations.
All: no transfer of a refusal direction; the human-written transfer result is for a tone direction.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to 'none'; no row bears on any refusal version. The relation is changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only' because Arditi et al. appears only in the introduction and related-work citations. The sentiment 'single direction is incomplete' result is a conceptual parallel to V4 but concerns a different construct, so it is not a verdict on V4. Table 4 subspace metrics are omitted from the rows, which is acceptable since they do not concern refusal.

versions.untested_parts: Refusal-direction measurement, refusal ablation or addition, and preservation of general capabilities.
Weight-edit ablation of refusal in released models.
Whether attacks suppress a refusal direction or training against ablation improves robustness.
Whether refusal is affine, cone-shaped, or distributed across multiple directions.
Whether harmfulness judgment is represented separately from refusal.
Transfer of a refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base and instruct models.
Effects of refusal-training method or timing on directionality.

relation.reason: Refusal appears only in three citations of Arditi et al. 2024 (intro lines 46-47, related work lines 172-173 and 239), each listing it as prior concept-direction or steering work. The refusal-direction claim itself is never discussed, so the reader's earlier 'discusses' is rightly overridden.

tranche.reason: The study is about sentiment-polarity directions and tone/audience residuals. It never derives, ablates, adds or uses a refusal direction, and it measures no refusal.

source_check.notes: All 20 sampled rows match Tables 3, 5, 6 and 14 and Section 7.2 exactly. Checkpoints are Meta-Llama-3-8B-Instruct, Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 and Gemma-7B-IT (Table 12). The record's authors_conclusion and test_reason are accurate. Off-topic for refusal_direction: its 'shared direction plus structured residual' result concerns sentiment, so at most it is an analogy to V4 in another concept.
